articles.title: Walking the Peak District, I discovered a wonderful rejection of the right’s monotone vision of England | John Harris
articles.summary: The landscape was striking, but so was the diversity of the hikers. We can make this the new normal – and we should. A fortnight or so ago, my two teenage kids and I set out on a three-night visit to the Peak District where temperatures were hovering at a comparatively tepid 28C.
body: The next bit might sound self-parodically Guardian-esque, but what the hell: in its own way, the most striking sight was the diversity of the scores of people rambling up, down and along. Women in their 20s wearing hijabs picnicked on giant rocks, while multiracial gaggles of young men attempted to race to the top; solo and shirtless white fitness freaks and retirement-age dog walkers took their places alongside them. With plenty of justification, country walking has long been typified as one of the most monoculturally white pursuits there is. But here – presumably because of the relatively close proximity of Manchester and Sheffield – things looked different.
points: The landscape was striking, but so was the diversity of the hikers.
We can make this the new normal – and we should.

articles.title: Quench your thirst! 20 perfect spritzes and shandies to try now – from kumquat to portergaff
articles.summary: Whether you love a traditional spritz or tend towards a wilder libation, this August there are bubbly and sophisticated drinks to suit every taste. This summer, UK web searches for “Hugo spritz”, an elderflower-flavoured aperitif, overtook searches for “Aperol spritz” for the first time.
body: Traditionally, the spritz is an Italian cocktail made from prosecco, a bitter aperitif or liqueur, and a splash of soda water to keep things steady. While Venetian bartenders are more likely to judge it by eye, there is a simple 3-2-1 formula for making a spritz at home: three parts prosecco, two parts liqueur and one part soda water. I’ve gone with 75ml/50ml/25ml – keep the same ratios to make a smaller (60ml/40ml/20ml) or larger (90ml/60ml/30ml) drink. Of course, you can then adjust it to make it stronger or weaker (I have been known to leave out the soda …).

If wine-based cocktails aren’t to your taste, shandy is also showing signs of a resurgence – Ocado sales have increased 40% year on year, and the craft brand Shandy Shack is now stocked in M&S. Being half beer, half soft drink, it is another summery thirst-quencher that is easy to make at home and (in theory) shouldn’t get you too sloshed.
So, here are 20 simple spritzes and shandies. Save your Malibu for a piña colada.
All recipes make one drink. Pour the liquids into a large glass with ice, stir briefly and garnish.

articles.title: The 7 Best Airbnbs in Morocco Include Stately Riads
articles.summary: An Airbnb in Morocco gives you lots of space, privacy, and (if you book one of our favorite riads) unique architectural charm. Here, seven favorites.
body: Wandering around Morocco’s medinas involves a bit of sensory overload. The small, winding alleyways are full of life: local artisans parade their crafts; spice merchants stand behind conical mounds of brightly colored saffron, paprika, and turmeric; women sell fresh herbs and Argan oil; young children on bikes weave through it all with almost unbelievable ease.

Once you look beyond it all, you begin to notice the streets themselves; specifically the heavy wooden doors, sometimes intricately carved, other times plain and unassuming. It’s behind these doors that the noise of the streets and souks stops. A few open into cafés or museums, but many of them lead into private homes—multi-floor spaces where windows and balconies overlook central courtyards filled with citrus trees, decorative tiling, and sparkling pools and fountains. Welcome to the Moroccan riad.
points: An Airbnb in Morocco gives you lots of space, privacy, and (if you book one of our favorite riads) unique architectural charm.

articles.title: How to make the perfect zaru soba, or cold soba noodles – recipe | Felicity Cloake's How to make the perfect
articles.summary: Hot days call for cool dinners, and these are Japan’s nutty, salty and sweet solution. Fiery or pickled accompaniments optional. Although every culture craves something different in hot weather – chilled beetroot soup in Lithuania, cooling buttermilk drinks in India, gazpacho in Spain – what many…
body: Zaru soba isn’t the only chilled noodle dish that Japan slurps in summer – Emiko Davies favours her mother’s somen (delicate wheat-flour strands), while Shota Nakajima makes a case for hiyashi chuka, a Chinese-inspired ramen salad. Sadly, though, spindly somen and fresh ramen are trickier to source in the UK than buckwheat soba, which can be found in many larger supermarkets.

Once cooled, the soba are best consumed immediately, but if you find they’ve started to tangle, give them a rinse under cold water to separate the strands, then drain them well again afterwards. Traditionally, soba are served on a flat bamboo straining mat called a zaru, but as long as you toss them well, a less picturesque plate or bowl is fine.

The proper way to eat zaru soba, according to Maehashi, is to “pick up a few strands of noodles and dip only the bottom half of them into the dipping sauce by simply lowering the chopsticks. Many people drop all the noodles they just picked up into the dipping sauce,” she adds, “but this is not a real gourmet way of eating buckwheat noodles. By dipping only part of the soba noodles in, you can taste the flavour of the noodles and enjoy it better.” So that’s you told.

articles.title: Stores are selling Halloween stuff in August. Time has lost all meaning | Dave Schilling
articles.summary: Capitalism and the climate crisis are conspiring to destroy the concept of seasons. I’ll take solace in my pumpkin spice. Happy spooky season, everyone! Get those jack-o’-lanterns out, because Halloween is just around the corner! Just kidding, no, it’s not.
body: It’s August, for God’s sake. Every day, I wake up to 90F weather – my skin moist with sweat and my eyelids stuck together. I can’t drink coffee on my porch without being consumed by an army of voracious mosquitoes that seem to find my blood to be the most delicious of all.

Why am I fuming about this? Even though I love Halloween, I’m mad because our glorious big-box overlords have declared, via careful inventory selection, that Halloween season has begun. In August. I find all of that unacceptable. It feels like a violation of the natural order, a realignment of one of the few glorious constants left in the world. I yearn to go back to the tidy order of holidays, where no two ever cross paths. At most, Halloween celebrations should start in late September. Not a month after Independence Day. I fear those days are done, that our world has irrevocably changed and I need to start getting ready to give in to the new normal.

articles.title: 17 Dreamy Miami Airbnbs in South Beach, Wynwood, and Beyond
articles.summary: These standout properties feature sprawling pools, sleek amenities, and walkable addresses.
body: I’ve always liked Miami best with a little room to spread out. I grew up coming here on family vacations, then came back for solo escapes, girls’ trips, and romantic weekends by the beach. Somehow, I still find myself falling for the city’s distinct combination of pastel Art Deco buildings, swaying palm trees, warm ocean air, and vibrant neighborhoods that feel like their own little universes.

Hotels can of course be fabulous here, but there’s something especially fun about having your own Miami address for a few days. A Miami Airbnb gives you the space to make coffee in your pajamas, open the doors to a pool or garden, pile everyone onto a sofa after the beach, and actually unpack instead of living out of a suitcase. I’m talking a leafy Coconut Grove hideaway, a glossy Brickell apartment with skyline views, or a colorful family house with a pool that has the potential to make leaving for dinner feel like a chore.
These are the Airbnbs I'd genuinely want to stay at in Miami—from breezy beach bases to character-filled homes that make a weekend away feel like a proper escape.

articles.title: How Our Editors Pick the Best New Restaurants
articles.summary: Editor in chief Jamila Robinson reflects on how the Best New Restaurants of 2026 gave us new ways to eat, gather, and see the world.
body: The question I’m asked most often is, “How does a restaurant get on ‘the list?’” The list can be any compilation of notable restaurants, including awards, star ratings, rankings, or media honors, such as Bon Appétit’s Best New Restaurants (the 2026 installment of our list publishes Monday, August 24th—check back in tomorrow).

My answers change every year, depending on the kinds of restaurants that open, the trend lines that emerge, and even the whispered wisdom at dinner parties or the buzz on social media. Earning a spot on the list can come down to thoughtful and seamless hospitality, such as a shawl offered in a cold dining room, or the box of chic reading glasses brought to me by a server who noticed I was doing a backbend trying to decipher a weeny menu typeface at a recent dinner in Stockholm.

articles.title: From Sophia Loren to Monica Bellucci, 20 Times Italian Bombshells Ruled the Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: From Sophia Loren to Monica Bellucci, we look back at the Venice Film Festival’s most stylish attendees from decades past.
body: Just as Cannes has its effortlessly chic French girls, Venice Film Festival has always been the undisputed domain of the Italian bombshell. Since the showcase’s inception nine decades ago, these impossibly glamorous women have shimmied off their private water taxis and onto the Lido in showstopping ball gowns, with dramatic cat eyes and lashings of mascara, their hair teased up to perfection and eye-wateringly expensive jewels draped around their necks. Among them were Fellini heroines like Claudia Cardinale; Michelangelo Antonioni’s bewitching muse Monica Vitti; the always elegant Sophia Loren; and Monica Bellucci, still the very definition of va-va-voom style.
As we count down to the event’s 83rd edition, we look back at their most dazzling moments from festivals past.

articles.title: Zoë Kravitz Experiments in a Long Misunderstood Denim Style
articles.summary: Harry Styles and Zoë Kravitz have a shared love of classic straight-leg jeans; but the actor strikes out in a more retro silhouette.
body: Zoë Kravitz knows good bottoms. Whether it’s The Row’s flowing Gala pants, Cou Cou Intimates bermudas, or the no-waistband style Still Here low-rider jeans, Kravitz has a regular rotation of contemporary classics that act as the foundation of her wardrobe. Now engaged to partner Harry Styles, the actor and her pop star husband-to-be have established they have a similar taste in denim: relaxed, usually straight-leg, deep blue.

Now back in New York before Styles takes on his mammoth 30-night residency at Madison Square Garden, Kravitz is experimented in a long maligned denim silhouette—one that Styles probably wouldn’t be up for incorporating into their coordinating couple style. Namely, a pair of light-wash blue cropped and kick flare jeans that sat ultra low on the waist.

articles.title: Ariana Grande and Ricky Álvarez Layer Up for an Even Harder Launch in London
articles.summary: In London for the Eternal Sunshine tour, Ariana Grande and boyfriend Ricky Álvarez are holding onto the last embers of British summertime, despite the temp.
body: The Eternal Sunshine tour has brought Ariana Grande to London for an ambitious 10-day residency. A city she’s long loved, of course Ari brought her rekindled flame Ricky Álvarez with her to enjoy the last embers of British summer.

While we’ve not hit a coordinating couple style rhythm just yet, they have proved their commitment to each other this time around with matching tattoos. During one of her first London shows, Grande debuted the script, “I do love you,” which sits just on her collarbone. It matches one that Alvarez has inked in a similar place.
There was a few months of speculation that Grande and Álvarez had reunited, with Grande coyly teasing their coupledom.
Grande and Álvarez became Instagram official last week, with a photo dump that featured several mirror selfies that showed them embracing.
